population.text: Patients with active CD55-deficient protein-losing enteropathy (CHAPLE disease) with hypoalbuminemia and confirmed biallelic CD55 loss-of-function mutation; enrolled subjects ranged from 3 to 19 years of age.

citations.quote: The efficacy and safety of VEOPOZ were evaluated in a single-arm study (NCT04209634) where outcomes were compared to pre-treatment data in patients with active CD55-deficient protein-losing enteropathy (PLE) who had hypoalbuminemia.
Ten patients ranging from 3 to 19 years of age (median of 8.5 years) were assessed for efficacy.

endpoint.text: Multi-component primary endpoint: normalization of serum albumin between Weeks 12 and 24 plus improvement in the 4 pre-specified clinical outcomes evaluable for improvement at baseline without worsening of the others after 24 weeks of treatment.

citations.quote: The pre-specified primary efficacy endpoint was a multi-component endpoint that includes both:
- Improvement in the 4 pre-specified clinical outcomes that are evaluable for improvement at baseline, without worsening of the others, after 24 weeks of treatment

The protocol-specified primary endpoint was the proportion of subjects who achieved both the normalization of albumin between Week 12 and Week 24 and the improvement in the pre-specified clinical outcomes.
Ten patients ranging from 3 to 19 years of age (median of 8.5 years) were assessed for efficacy.

result.text: All 10 (100%) subjects achieved normalization of serum albumin and demonstrated improvement in clinical signs/symptoms (100% efficacy; 90% CI: 74.1%, 100%). All 10 achieved serum albumin ≥ 3.5 g/dL by Week 12; median time to normalization 15.5 days (95% CI: 8 to 28).

citations.quote: Based on the pre-specified multi-component primary endpoint, all 10 (100%) subjects with active disease at baseline achieved normalization of serum albumin and demonstrated improvement in clinical signs and symptoms evaluable for improvement at baseline, without worsening of the others after 24 weeks of treatment, indicating 100% efficacy (90% CI: 74.1%, 100%) (Table 24) below. As noted in Section

The median time for serum albumin to reach at least 3.5 g/dL was 15.5 days (N=10; 95% CI: 8 to 28). All 10 patients achieved normalization by Week 12 and maintained serum albumin concentrations within the normal range through at least 72 weeks of treatment (Figure 1).

indication.text: VEOPOZ is a complement inhibitor indicated for the treatment of adult and pediatric patients 1 year of age and older with CD55-deficient protein-losing enteropathy (PLE), also known as CHAPLE disease.

target_moa.text: Pozelimab-bbfg is a human IgG4P monoclonal antibody directed against terminal complement protein C5; it inhibits terminal complement activation by blocking cleavage of C5 into C5a and C5b, thereby blocking formation of the membrane-attack complex (C5b-C9).

citations.quote: Pozelimab-bbfg is a human, monoclonal immunoglobulin G4P (IgG4P) antibody directed against the terminal complement protein C5 that inhibits terminal complement activation by blocking cleavage of C5 into C5a (anaphylatoxin) and C5b, thereby blocking the formation of the membrane-attack complex (C5b-C9, a structure mediating cell lysis).

Pozelimab-bbfg, a complement inhibitor, is a recombinant monoclonal antibody (IgG4 isotype). Pozelimab-bbfg is produced by recombinant DNA technology in Chinese Hamster Ovary (CHO) cell suspension culture and has an approximate molecular weight of 145 kDa.

key_safety.text: In 10 treated patients, the most common adverse reactions (reported in two or more patients) were upper respiratory tract infection (30%), fracture (30%), urticaria (20%), and alopecia (20%). The most serious risk is life-threatening and fatal meningococcal infections.

requirement.text: 4490-1: Re-evaluate the current anti-drug antibody (ADA) assay to improve sensitivity in the presence of trough drug levels; validation assessments to include selectivity, system suitability, hemolysis effects, and statistical distribution/outlier evaluation.

citations.quote: 4490-1 Re-evaluate the current anti-drug antibody (ADA) assay with the goal of improving sensitivity in the presence of the trough level of drug expected to be present during sampling.
